title: Modern Realistic
premise: The real world. No powers, no magic, no chosen ones. Just people, cities, choices, and consequences.

lore.title: Calder Central Hospital
lore.text: The city's largest hospital, a fourteen-story complex on Mercer Avenue. Its Level I trauma center takes most gunshot and vehicle crash cases in the county. Weekend wait times in the main emergency department often run four to six hours.

lore.title: Westbrook Transit Hub
lore.text: Calder's central rail and bus interchange, serving three metro lines and eleven bus routes. Police and contracted security patrol the concourse around the clock. Pickpocketing and fare disputes make up most daily reports.

lore.title: Lantern Row
lore.text: A four-block nightlife district of bars, clubs, and late diners on the river side of downtown. City ordinance requires bars to close by 2 a.m. Weekend crowds bring steady noise complaints and a heavy patrol presence.

lore.title: Eastfield
lore.text: A residential neighborhood of brick rowhouses and small corner shops, home to about forty thousand people. Most residents commute downtown by bus. The community association meets monthly at the Eastfield branch library.

lore.title: Halvard University Campus
lore.text: A public research university of about twenty-two thousand students on the north edge of the city. Its medical school shares clinical rotations with Calder Central Hospital. Campus police handle on-campus incidents and assist the city department off campus.

lore.title: Calder Police Department
lore.text: The municipal police force, roughly 1,400 sworn officers across six precincts. Runs a homicide unit, a narcotics division, and a public information office. Civilian oversight comes from a review board appointed by the city council.

lore.title: Metro Transit Authority
lore.text: The public agency that runs Calder's rail lines, buses, and paratransit service. Funded by fares, a regional sales tax, and state grants. Known for recurring weekend service cuts and long-running disputes over maintenance contracts.

lore.title: The Brannock Syndicate
lore.text: An organized crime network working through trucking, illegal lending, and nightlife security contracts. Its leadership is not public record. Investigators have linked it to two bar owners on Lantern Row and a shell company in the port district.

lore.title: Calder City Council
lore.text: Eleven elected members who set the municipal budget, zoning rules, and bar licensing. Meetings are public and streamed online. Current debates center on housing density in Eastfield and a review of late-night licensing exemptions.

lore.title: City of Calder
lore.text: A population of about 610,000 spread across 84 square miles on a river delta with a working port. Downtown holds most office jobs, while the outer districts rely on bus and rail links to reach them. Income gaps between neighborhoods are wide.

lore.title: Metro Fares and Transfers
lore.text: A single metro fare costs $2.75 and is paid with a reloadable transit card. Transfers are valid for ninety minutes. Riders without valid fare receive a civil citation under city ordinance rather than an arrest.

lore.title: Lantern Row Licensing Rules
lore.text: Bars and clubs on Lantern Row hold city licenses requiring last call at 1:45 a.m. and closing by 2 a.m. Violations can bring fines, temporary suspension, or revocation after a hearing before the council's licensing committee.

lore.title: Emergency Intake Policy
lore.text: Calder Central's emergency department triages patients by medical acuity, not arrival order. Patients under police custody or a hold are treated in a separate secured bay. Records requests go through the hospital's health information office.

lore.title: Dr. Mireille Acheampong
lore.text: Attending emergency physician at Calder Central who runs the night trauma shift with a firm hand. Cautious with police requests and protective of patient privacy. Trained at Halvard's medical school and still teaches its residents.

lore.title: Sergeant Tobias Quillen
lore.text: Patrol sergeant for the Eastfield precinct with twenty-two years on the force. Tracks overtime budgets closely and is slow to trust outsiders. Quietly skeptical of Brannock Syndicate influence on Lantern Row.

lore.title: Nico Tanaka-Brandt
lore.text: Dispatch supervisor at the Metro Transit Authority control center in Westbrook. Monitors service disruptions and fare-gate complaints around the clock. Has filed three public records requests about maintenance contract overruns.

lore.title: Councilmember Hollis Maren
lore.text: Fourth-term council member representing Eastfield and the river wards. Pushes for housing density and transit funding. Publicly opposes the late-night licensing exemptions that Lantern Row bar owners have lobbied for.
